To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed autoencoder is a powerful tool for representation learning in the domain of 3D geometry and (ii) GMMs trained with the latent space of the proposed AEs produce the most faithful and diverse samples.

1) the latent space learned by our AE is a good representation of the underlying distribution of shapes, 2) the latent space is well-suited for generative modeling, and 3) GMMs trained on the latent space produce the most realistic and diverse samples.

1) our AE network is the first to learn compact, disentangled and meaningful representations of point clouds; 2) our AE-based GMM is a state-of-the-art generative model for point clouds; 3) the latent space of the AE can be used as a semantic part space for editing and interpolation; 4) the latent space can be used as an input space for GANs, improving their performance on raw point clouds.

learning representations of 3D shapes that enable basic shape editing and shape generation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple AE architecture can be used to learn representations that allow to perform basic shape editing, and that the latent space of AEs is a natural space for GMM training.
, for point clouds, a good generative model is not necessarily a good representation, and vice versa.
, for 3D data, a simple AE trained with L2 loss can learn representations that are better than GANs for generative modeling, while being more stable and easier to train.
